name: DavesLastMassage
source:
Sounds like ship and smells like hell. Ring any bells? 
 
 *Shit* was exactly what he smelled like. And not cat, dog or bird. I'm talking big guns, your average Mexicalli diner after a dose of their famous chilli sauce. 
 
 I do n't know what happened to the poor guy. Slumped in a single seater cotton couch with a Heiniken light between his thighs. 
 
 If I had to take a guess I'd say he could n't handle his drink. But we both knew that was a lie. I knew exactly what happened to err... What's his name again? 
 
 I inched forward and slipped the fat leather wallet from his jacket pocket. `` Dave?'' At least that's what his licence said. 
 
 Dave was scorched black, he looked nothing like the young dude in the picture. By his feet were a packet of fags and a lighter. I snatched em up for later, despite the edge of one being nibbled on. 
 
 Leaning back up, I paused. A tag on the bottom of the chair read,'*Tony's Massage 360*' 
 
 So, shit, beer, ciggies and a massage chair. 
 
 It's no surprise Dave had a shocking time. 
 
 I slipped out a fresh one and sparked it up. My phone buzzed: `` you done?'' I smirked and flicked back, `` Cat's in the bag. Dial the pigs and send over the goods.'' 
 
 Glancing at Dave I almost felt bad for the poor sod. `` Next time bruv, do n't borrow money off the godfather.'' 
 
 His apartment door shut quietly behind me. I realised how ironic my words had been, but they were more for me than Dave.
retelling:
From the perspective of Dave, the Deceased Man:

In the dimly lit confines of Tony's Massage 360, I found myself in an unexpected predicament. The last thing I remembered was accepting a job offer from someone I owed a substantial debt, and now here I lay, sprawled across a single-seater cotton couch that doubled as a massage chair.

I could feel the burning sensation emanating from my body, a testament to the recent gunshots that had left me lifeless in this small, claustrophobic space. The air was thick with the pungent aroma of burnt flesh, reminiscent of a Mexicalli diner after a dose of their famous chilli sauce.

I vaguely recalled the sound of footsteps approaching and a hand rummaging through my pockets, stealing my wallet and cigarettes. I couldn't protest; I was already beyond salvation. The tag on the massage chair identified this place as Tony's Massage 360, but I never got to ask why I ended up here or who brought me here.

A text message buzzed in my pocket, confirming the completion of a task, a task that cost me my life. I couldn't help but feel a sense of regret for the choices I had made, for the debts I had accumulated. As darkness enveloped me, I was left to ponder the cruel irony of owing one's life to another.

In the quiet stillness that followed, there was only one sound that pierced through the silence - the sound of my own heartbeat slowly fading away, until it was silenced forever.
